![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221961/assets/3c2035d50b823b9bcbeb3ae8cf698df9a25c95a289c5a6f35054269dc920088d.png)

Consider the vector field $F$ shown above, and let $C$ be the path where the curve is traversed from $A$ to $B.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$

II. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$

III. ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ gives the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along $C:$

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statement I is true, while statement II is false. It's clear from the picture below that $F$ assists the motion of the particle as it moves from $A$ to $B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221961/assets/dfec76b47e8508a57e18440a72986bcae8e2bd19559bd0915ea4530e0b08b4f6.png)

 
So, ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- Statement III is false. It's clear from the picture below that if we reverse the orientation of $C,$ then $F$ works against the motion of the particle as it moves from $B$ to $A.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221961/assets/58e3efc39d0aee02d14e7c80c7355c37a1f28b6f0f54ff7102553e3a6ffc17cf.png)

 
So, ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
